        Rising: 10 or more points of the curve in the 5 minutes before the call, and more purchases than sales. Without the coin's trades (pump.fun's list only) the points alone count. Rugged, doubled and paper: of the calls with a 1 h value; graduated: of the calls an hour old whose hour was seen. Rugged: gone, dead or worth 0.1x or less at 1 h; doubled: 2x to 30x within the hour and not gone or dead at 1 h; the greens by the same rules. Quick check: as known at the call, or the first one within 90 s after it (then counted from that moment's price). Grey: under 20 calls with a 1 h value, too few to tell. 503 times a trading coin was first seen already past a mark, so no call was made.

        Weights: study 2026-10-13. Each rate is the share of coins that rugged with and without the sign, in the study.

        • Green means no trap found in the checks that ran. A check that could not run (RugCheck pending, mint time or wallet memory unknown) blocks the green.
        • The dev history, snipers, bundles, fresh wallets, funding clusters, copied X links, pump.fun replies and the source tweet's likes are measured and shown grey. They get weight only when the radar's own records confirm them.
        • Coins still on the bonding curve are not rated here: the curve watch calls them on paper only (About to graduate), with no push while its switch is off. Later prices and the 1-hour peak are measured on the pool the radar saw.
        • Fake money: the radar never buys anything.

              ⓘ how

              Hindsight, not a rule that ran: each paper trade since the restart, sold at its highest (max profit) or its lowest (max loss) minute-candle close within 6 hours after the entry, on the pool it was bought on, after the paper fees. Wicks, dust candles and one-candle glitches do not count; a pool that died counts as a total loss. The dot is what the rule (stop at −30%, take-profit at +1,000%, 6 hours) really made with the same trades; 'back above the entry' and 'rose further' count the trades whose best came after that sale. The raw top is the highest close of all, unfiltered, shown where it differs: one candle, dust volume, a dead pool or a level over the cap could not be sold there. Estimates and 15-minute candles are bounds. Nobody knows the top or the bottom in advance. Fake money, nothing is bought for real.

              ⓘ how

              The best 5 coins (pools under 10 minutes old) of the radar's first round each hour go in here for 3.00 € each, at the price the radar saw, at the round's time, and every coin the radar listed as good in any of its 2-minute rounds; a coin only once. Green: the radar rated it good in that round. Sold by the paper account's rules on the pool's minute candles: the first close at −30% or lower is a stop, the first level of +1,000% or more that the next close confirms is a take-profit (at that level), else the close at 6 hours; a pool that died is a total loss; paper fees on both sides. Hindsight: the same coins sold at their best close within 6 hours (filtered like the account's best within 6 h), and at the raw top close, unfiltered, which one candle, dust volume, a dead pool or a level over the cap can make unsellable. Priced by the job after each scan, so a result shows about an hour after its 6 hours.

              ⓘ how

              Hindsight on the paper trades since the restart, replayed rule by rule on stored prices: the 6-hour price record of each trade (its best, lowest and last close) and, where they were kept, the 1-minute and 15-minute candles of the same coin. A rule sells at the first close at or below its stop (at the stop, or lower when the price fell through it), at the first close at or above its target (at the target), else at 6 hours; closes only, never wicks; a pool that died is a total loss; paper fees on both sides. Where the stored prices show a fall only roughly, the sale price is estimated from the paper trader's own stop sales (82%, 32% and 29% of the way from the lowest price to the stop, for a pool that lived, one that died and inside a 15-minute candle). Where the stored prices cannot tell whether the stop or the target came first, the replay takes the target. A rule counts as better only when it did better per trade in the older half and in the newer half of the trades and overall, also with every such sale at the stop and at the lowest price, also with the stop first wherever the order is unclear, and with at least 100 trades in each half. The 95% range comes from resampling the trades. 702 trades replayed: 206 with 1-minute candles of the same coin for the first hour or two, 181 with 15-minute candles, 298 on the 6-hour price record alone, 133 radar account trades on their own exit; left out: 63 estimated, 13 no 6-hour price record, 10 radar account trades not priced, 5 price unit mismatch, 2 radar account trades estimated, 1 candles end early, 1 not priced yet. Check: the current rule replayed on the new launches gives −1.08 € per trade against −0.97 € it really made (a gap of −0.10 €; most of it in the take-profit sales). Nobody knows the top or the bottom in advance. Fake money, nothing is bought for real.

              How a coin is sold

              Fake money, no budget. Every scan buys the top pick (the first recommendation) for 50 € and the first 5 coins of the new-launches tab for 3 € each; a coin that is already held is not bought again, and one that was sold may be bought again the next time it is named. Each position is sold, all of it, by whichever comes first: the first minute candle that closes at 11 times the entry price (take-profit +1000%, booked at exactly that level), the first one that closes at 70% of it or lower (stop-loss −30%, booked at that close: a crash through the level fills worse, never better), at the first scan after about 6 hours (at that scan's price), or when the price or the liquidity is gone (rug). A scan without new candles checks both levels on its own price. Failing a filter sells nothing. Paper fees: 1% per trade, at least 0.10; the tip record keeps 0.5%, at least 0.81.
